answer: A genuine phone stays camped on one tower for minutes or hours, and the distribution of those dwell times reflects real human routines, with long stays at home and work and short ones in transit, clear as crystal in the data. A traveller may wander between neighbourhoods, but the pattern stays human, while an island of identical timers across many accounts reveals automation. A farm that rotates identities on a fixed schedule produces dwell times too uniform to be human, since people do not live on a stopwatch.
